prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Fle fro the pres, and dwelle with sothefastnesse, Suffise thin owen thing, thei it be smal; For hord hath hate, and clymbyng tykelnesse, Prees hath envye, and wele blent overal. Savour no more thanne the byhove schal; Reule weel thiself, that other folk canst reede; And trouthe schal delyvere, it is no drede. Tempest the nought al croked to redresse, In trust of hire that tourneth as a bal. Myche wele stant in litel besynesse; Bywar therfore to spurne ayeyns an al; Stryve not as doth the crokke with the wal. Daunte thiself, that dauntest otheres dede; And trouthe shal delyvere, it is no drede. That the is sent, receyve in buxumnesse; The wrestlyng for the worlde axeth a fal. Here is non home, here nys but wyldernesse. Forth, pylgryme, forth! forth, beste, out of thi stal! Know thi contré! loke up! thonk God of al! Hold the heye weye, and lat thi gost the lede; And trouthe shal delyvere, it is no drede. Therfore, thou Vache, leve thine olde wrechednesse; Unto the world leve now to be thral. Crie hym mercy, that of hys hie godnesse Made the of nought, and in espec{.i}al Draw unto hym, and pray in general For the, and eke for other, hevenelyche mede; And trouthe schal delyvere, it is no drede.

prompts.L3:
Please expand the following bullet points into a complete, well-structured text:

- Flee public acclaim, live truthfully, and be content with your own possessions, however small.
- Avoid greed, ambition, and worldly prosperity, which bring hatred, insecurity, envy, and blindness.
- Govern yourself before advising others, and do not exhaust yourself trying to correct every wrong.
- Accept what comes with humility, resist enslavement to the world, and let your spirit guide you on life’s pilgrimage.
- Turn toward God, seek mercy, pray for yourself and others, and trust that truth will deliver you.
prompts.L4:
Please expand the following two-sentence summary into a complete text:

The poem addresses the dangers of greed, ambition, worldly struggle, and self-deception through direct moral counsel urging contentment, humility, self-discipline, and trust in God. Its central message is that steadfast truth and spiritual obedience bring deliverance, freeing the pilgrim from worldly bondage and guiding the soul toward heaven.
prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Fle, Suffise, For

outputs.L2:
Leave the crowd behind and live in honesty.  
Be satisfied with what is yours, however little it may be.  
Hoarding breeds hatred, and ambition brings uncertainty;  
Fame provokes envy, while prosperity blinds everyone.  
Desire no more than necessity requires.  
Govern yourself well, since you know how to counsel others;  
Truth will set you free—of that there is no doubt.

Do not exhaust yourself trying to straighten everything crooked,  
Depending on Fortune, which spins around like a ball.  
Great happiness may be found in a life of few concerns.  
Take care not to kick against a sharp point,  
And do not struggle like an earthen pot striking a wall.  
Master yourself, you who would judge and restrain others’ actions;  
Truth will set you free—of that there is no doubt.

Accept obediently whatever is sent to you.  
Anyone who wrestles with the world invites a fall.  
This place is not our home; it is only a wilderness.  
Go on, pilgrim—move forward! Beast, leave your stall!  
Recognize your true homeland, look upward, and thank God for everything.  
Keep to the high road and allow your spirit to guide you;  
Truth will set you free—of that there is no doubt.

Therefore, Vache, abandon your former wretched way of life.  
No longer remain enslaved to the world.  
Beg mercy from the one who, in his supreme goodness,  
Created you from nothing. Above all, draw near to him,  
And pray for heavenly reward, both for yourself  
And for everyone else as well;  
Truth will set you free—of that there is no doubt.
outputs.L3:
Flee public acclaim and resist the desire to be admired. Instead, live truthfully and be content with what is yours, however modest it may be. True peace does not depend on abundance or recognition, but on an honest life and a grateful heart.

Guard yourself against greed, ambition, and the pursuit of worldly prosperity. These promises of success often bring hatred, insecurity, envy, and spiritual blindness. The more tightly you cling to status and possessions, the more easily they can rule you and disturb your peace.

Before advising or correcting others, learn to govern yourself. Attend first to your own conduct, motives, and weaknesses. Do not exhaust yourself trying to remedy every injustice or fault you encounter; wisdom lies in knowing what you can change, what you must endure, and when silence is better than interference.

Accept what comes with humility, without surrendering your freedom to the values of the world. Refuse to become enslaved by possessions, reputation, or fear. Let your spirit guide you through life’s pilgrimage, keeping your attention fixed on what is lasting rather than what quickly passes away.

Above all, turn toward God. Seek mercy, pray for your own needs and failings, and remember others in your prayers as well. Place your trust in divine truth, for truth brings clarity, freedom, and deliverance to those who faithfully follow it.
outputs.L4:
The poem offers a sustained moral reflection on the dangers that confront human beings in their earthly lives. Greed, ambition, and the restless desire for worldly success are presented not as paths to genuine fulfillment, but as forms of bondage. The pursuit of wealth, status, and power distracts people from what is spiritually valuable and draws them into endless conflict, anxiety, and dissatisfaction. Because worldly desires can disguise themselves as reasonable needs or worthy ambitions, the poem also warns against self-deception. A person may believe that they are acting wisely while actually being ruled by pride, appetite, or fear.

In response to these dangers, the speaker gives direct moral counsel. The reader is urged to practice contentment rather than covet what others possess, to choose humility instead of seeking superiority, and to exercise self-discipline in the face of temptation. Such virtues require constant vigilance, since the struggle is not only against external pressures but also against weaknesses within the self. True freedom therefore comes from mastering selfish desires rather than satisfying them. By accepting limits and resisting the attractions of worldly glory, the individual can recover a clearer sense of purpose.

Trust in God is central to this spiritual discipline. Human plans, possessions, and achievements are temporary and uncertain, whereas divine truth provides a firm and lasting foundation. The poem encourages the faithful person to remain obedient even during hardship, trusting that suffering and sacrifice are not meaningless. Steadfastness in truth protects the soul from corruption and allows the believer to endure the trials of life without surrendering to despair or temptation.

Ultimately, the poem presents human life as a pilgrimage. The world can imprison the pilgrim through desire, pride, and illusion, but spiritual obedience opens the way to deliverance. Contentment loosens the hold of greed; humility defeats ambition; self-discipline restrains destructive impulses; and faith directs the traveler toward the proper destination. The poem’s central message is therefore both cautionary and hopeful: those who reject false worldly promises, remain faithful to truth, and place their trust in God can be freed from earthly bondage and guided toward salvation and heaven.
outputs.L5:
### Fle, Suffise, For

Ordene **Fle**, **Suffise** og **For** kan oppfattes som små fragmenter av språk. Alene virker de kanskje ufullstendige, men de viser hvordan korte lyder og bokstavkombinasjoner kan få mening gjennom sammenheng. **For** kan innlede en forklaring, mens **Suffise** minner om suffikser – endelser som endrer betydningen eller formen til et ord. **Fle** kan på sin side være begynnelsen på et navn, en lyd eller et nytt, oppdiktet begrep. Sammen illustrerer de at språk er fleksibelt: Selv enkle fragmenter kan vekke tanker, skape assosiasjoner og bli utgangspunktet for en historie.
